definitions.explanation: The speed at which music is played.
The speed or pace of an activity or conversation.

examples.japanese: テンポが{速|はや}い{曲|きょく}だ。
テンポを{上|あ}げて{演奏|えんそう}する。
もう{少|すこ}しテンポを{落|お}として{弾|ひ}いてみてください。
examples.english: Try playing it at a slightly slower tempo.

examples.japanese: {会話|かいわ}のテンポがいい。
examples.english: The conversation flows at a good pace.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}のテンポが{上|あ}がってきた。
examples.english: The pace of work has picked up.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}はテンポがよくて、{最後|さいご}まで{飽|あ}きずに{見|み}られた。
examples.english: This movie had great pacing and I was engaged until the end.

notes:
テンポ refers to the speed of music or the pace of activities and conversation.

ETYMOLOGY:
From Italian "tempo" (time).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- テンポが{速|はや}い: fast tempo/pace
- テンポが{遅|おそ}い: slow tempo/pace
- テンポを{上|あ}げる: to speed up
- テンポを{落|お}とす: to slow down
- テンポがいい: good rhythm/flow

USAGE:
Used for both musical tempo and general pace:
- {曲|きょく}のテンポ: tempo of a song
- {会話|かいわ}のテンポ: pace of conversation
- {仕事|しごと}のテンポ: work pace

RELATED:
- リズム: rhythm
